setup: One dumbbell in one hand at your side
Other hand on your hip or by your head
execution: Let it slide down the side of your leg
Pull yourself upright with the other side
Do all your reps, then switch hands
faults: Don't bounce out of the bottom

notes: Bend only as far as you can control; this is a small range.
Hold one dumbbell only. A weight in each hand balances out and takes the work away.
Some coaches prefer side planks or suitcase carries, which work the same muscles without bending the spine. Either is a reasonable choice.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Bodyweight side bend
regressions.reason: Learn the range and the straight sideways path with no load.

progressions.name: Heavier dumbbell
progressions.reason: Small jumps, with the bend still slow and controlled.

substitutions.name: Suitcase carry
substitutions.reason: Same side-of-waist muscles, resisting the bend while walking.

substitutions.name: Side plank
substitutions.reason: Holds the side of the waist with the spine still.

substitutions.name: Cable side bend
substitutions.reason: Stack-loaded side bend with smaller load steps.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Trunk work that resists twisting instead.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at waist height, figure facing the camera with one dumbbell in the right hand and the left hand on the hip. The sideways bend reads only from the front.

keyPositions.label: Upright
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, feet hip-width. Dumbbell hanging at the right side, arm straight. Left hand on the hip. Shoulders level.

keyPositions.label: Bend
keyPositions.describe: Torso bent sideways toward the dumbbell, which has slid down to about knee level along the outside of the leg. Hips stay over the feet; no forward lean or twist.

ikHints: Feet and pelvis fixed in every frame
Loaded arm stays straight; the dumbbell tracks along the leg
emphasise: Straight sideways path, no lean forward
The far side of the waist pulls you back up
